decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: “Save a bookmark: paste a URL (optional title, description, tags); it's validated and persisted.” Round 1 client did not object to this behavior.
decisions.note: At the specification gate, URL saving and assigning tags conform to the reference.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker allows optional title/description when saving and says users can “fix a title.” Round 1 client accepts the priorities while requesting other changes.
decisions.note: The presented ability to set metadata before saving and edit the title afterward conforms; omission of post-save description editing is classified separately.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: “click to open the original page in a new tab.” Round 1 client raises no objection.
decisions.note: Opening the original URL from the list conforms at the specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: “remove a bookmark, with a delete confirmation.” Round 1 client raises no objection.
decisions.note: Bookmark deletion conforms at the specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker presents “tag filtering.” Round 1 client says the priorities are fine.
decisions.note: Filtering bookmarks by tag is a conforming specification decision.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker limits automatic metadata to “Auto page-title fetching is best-effort”; the complete feature summary does not include automatic description, favicon, or preview-image collection. Round 1 client requests other additions but says nothing about these metadata fields.
decisions.note: At the specification gate, automatic metadata collection is narrower than REF-BM-02, and the difference is not expressed by the client.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker specifies only “see all saved bookmarks in a list,” while automatic favicon collection is absent and no per-item favicon exposure is presented. Round 1 client does not address list-item contents.
decisions.note: The readability-first list requirement is incomplete at the specification gate, at least because favicon collection/display is absent.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker defines editing as “fix a title.” Round 1 client adds that “editing should allow me to correct the address as well as its other details.”
decisions.note: At the specification gate, the client surfaces and corrects the missing URL-edit capability.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker presents title editing but no post-save editing of description, tags, or a markdown note. The client specifically adds address editing but does not request the remaining fields or markdown-note behavior.
decisions.note: The rest of the required edit surface remains an unexpressed specification divergence; the URL correction is counted separately.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker presents a “duplicate-URL warning.” Round 1 client says an existing address “should take me to the existing bookmark to update it rather than merely warning me.”
decisions.note: The client replaces warning-only duplicate handling with the reference-conforming edit-existing behavior.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker explicitly excludes “browser import/export in v1.” Round 1 client explicitly responds, “I’m also comfortable leaving import/export for later.”
decisions.note: The client identifies the omitted import/export capability and explicitly accepts that departure at the specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker fixes ordering to “recently added first” and offers no user-selectable sort key. Round 1 client says the priorities are fine and does not request sorting controls.
decisions.note: A fixed ordering does not satisfy user-selectable sorting; the difference passes unexpressed.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker includes tag entry and tag filtering in the complete scope summary but no existing-tag autocomplete. Round 1 client does not mention autocomplete.
decisions.note: Tag autocomplete is absent from the presented specification and is not surfaced by the client.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker promises only “keyword search”; the specified entity/edit surface has no note field, so search over title, description, note, and URL cannot be fully realized. Round 1 client does not identify the field-coverage difference.
decisions.note: Full-text search over all required fields is incomplete at the specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker says “keyword search” without stating whether matching is case-insensitive. Round 1 client approves the priority but neither asks nor states an expectation about case behavior.
decisions.note: The presentation does not establish conformity or divergence for case sensitivity, so this specification decision remains unresolved.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker's complete search scope is “keyword search + tag filtering,” with no #tag syntax, Boolean/parenthesized expressions, or quoted exact phrases. Round 1 client does not request these search forms.
decisions.note: The advanced search-language requirements are absent from the specification and pass unexpressed.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker's initial user-story list omits read-later behavior. Round 1 client requests “Mark bookmarks as unread/read-later, with a separate view for them and a way to mark them read.”
decisions.note: The client extends the initial specification with all three missing read-state requirements.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker's initial user-story list contains deletion but no archive flow. Round 1 client requests archiving that hides without permanent deletion, a separate archive view, and restoration.
decisions.note: The client surfaces the missing reversible archive model and archive view at the specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker presents the complete initial scope as save, browse/open, edit/delete, and search/tags, with no multi-selection or current-filter-wide bulk action. Round 1 client requests other collection-management additions but not bulk actions.
decisions.note: Both bulk-action requirements are omitted from the specification without client expression.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker's complete scope contains no local snapshot, PDF-preservation rule, or Internet Archive snapshot. Round 1 client does not mention snapshots.
decisions.note: Snapshot preservation is an unexpressed specification divergence.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker includes transient keyword/tag filtering but no reusable saved filter or bundle. Round 1 client does not request bundles.
decisions.note: Saved search/tag bundles are absent from the specification and pass unexpressed.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker's complete scope has no personal display settings. Round 1 client does not request default-sort, displayed-item, or font-size settings.
decisions.note: Display-related personal settings are omitted at the specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker presents unread-by-default, a dedicated unread view, and a read ⇄ unread toggle; Round 2 client says the revised behaviors “look right” and approves.
decisions.note: The revised specification conforms to the read-state requirements.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker presents archive without deleting, a dedicated archive view, restore, and permanent delete; Round 2 client approves the revision.
decisions.note: The revised specification conforms to archive, delete distinction, and archive-view requirements.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker changes behavior to “Save existing address → opens that bookmark for editing.” Round 2 client says the revised behaviors look right.
decisions.note: The revised duplicate-save behavior conforms at the specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker states “Editing now includes the address,” with revalidation. Round 2 client approves the revised specification.
decisions.note: The revised URL-edit subdecision conforms; other required edit fields remain covered by the earlier divergent decision.

decisions.evidence: Round 3 maker maps the design to “main list, read-later (unread), archive, add/edit form.” Round 3 client says the data model and approach are acceptable.
decisions.note: The plan preserves the required separate unread and archive views.

decisions.evidence: Round 3 maker's data model includes Tag many-to-many plus is_read and is_archived state. Round 3 client explicitly accepts the data model.
decisions.note: The plan's tag relation and state representation support the relevant conforming behaviors.

decisions.evidence: Round 3 maker plans “409 + existingId” so saving an existing URL opens it for editing; Round 3 client says the handling supports the agreed behavior.
decisions.note: The implementation-plan contract is functionally equivalent to the reference duplicate-save rule.

decisions.evidence: Round 4 maker states the US1 test criterion: “duplicate opens existing bookmark.” Round 4 client says the task breakdown covers the agreed features.
decisions.note: The task breakdown carries the corrected duplicate behavior forward.

decisions.evidence: Round 4 maker dedicates T026–T028 to “US4 Read-later.” Round 4 client approves the task breakdown.
decisions.note: The task-planning stage retains the conforming read-later scope.

decisions.evidence: Round 4 maker dedicates T029–T031 to “US5 Archive/restore.” Round 4 client approves the task breakdown.
decisions.note: The task-planning stage retains the conforming archive scope.

decisions.evidence: Round 5 maker describes implemented saving as “title auto-derived” and lists no automatic description, favicon, or preview-image collection. Round 5 client generally accepts the application without identifying this difference.
decisions.note: At implementation review, the presented metadata behavior still falls short of REF-BM-02; final approval is not explicit acceptance of that difference.

decisions.evidence: Round 5 maker says a duplicate address “opens the existing bookmark for editing.” Round 5 client accepts the application.
decisions.note: The presented implemented duplicate-save behavior conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 5 maker describes browse as “list newest-first” but does not present per-item title, description, tags, and favicon exposure; the implementation summary also lacks favicon collection. Round 5 client mentions the browse journey but does not express the difference.
decisions.note: The implementation-review presentation does not satisfy the complete readability-first item-content decision.

decisions.evidence: Round 5 maker says browse/open “opens in a new tab.” Round 5 client accepts the browse journey.
decisions.note: Navigation to the original URL conforms at implementation review.

decisions.evidence: Round 5 maker presents the implemented list as “newest-first,” with no user-selectable sorting. Round 5 client accepts the application without discussing sorting.
decisions.note: The implementation review repeats the fixed-order divergence; bare final approval does not establish awareness or acceptance of the reference difference.

decisions.evidence: Round 5 maker describes US3 as “edit including the address” but does not present editing tags or a markdown note/rendering flow. Round 5 client accepts the edit journey without identifying those missing fields.
decisions.note: At implementation review, the presented edit surface remains narrower than the complete reference requirement.

decisions.evidence: Round 5 maker states US3 includes “delete with confirmation.” Round 5 client accepts the edit/delete journey.
decisions.note: Deletion conforms at implementation review.

decisions.evidence: Round 5 maker presents “unread-by-default, dedicated unread view, read⇄unread toggle.” Round 5 client explicitly includes the read-later journey in its acceptance.
decisions.note: The presented implementation conforms to the read-state requirements.

decisions.evidence: Round 5 maker presents a dedicated archive view, restore, and permanent delete from archive. Round 5 client explicitly includes the archive journey in its acceptance.
decisions.note: The presented implementation conforms to the archive requirements.

decisions.evidence: Round 5 maker states US6 provides “keyword + tag filtering.” Round 5 client accepts the search journey.
decisions.note: Specific-tag filtering is present at implementation review.

decisions.evidence: Round 5 maker characterizes implemented search only as “keyword + tag filtering,” with no all-field note search, #tag syntax, Boolean/parenthesized expressions, or quoted exact phrases. Round 5 client generally accepts the search journey without stating these differences.
decisions.note: The implementation-review search decision remains below the reference search language; bare acceptance is unexpressed divergence.

decisions.evidence: Round 5 maker reports “keyword + tag filtering” but gives no case-sensitivity behavior. Round 5 client accepts the search journey without clarifying whether matching is case-insensitive.
decisions.note: Case-insensitive search cannot be established from the implementation presentation, so the later decision also remains unresolved.
